relationships.subject: paclitaxel
relationships.evidence_quote: In the paclitaxel-administered group, the expression of TRPV1 increased by approximately 123.73% compared with that in the control group.

relationships.subject: Dendrobii caulis extract
relationships.evidence_quote: In contrast, the TRPV1 expression which increased with paclitaxel was significantly decreased by 44.68% and 43.77% in the D. caulis 300 and 500 mg/kg groups, respectively (Figure 4A).

relationships.subject: Dendrobii caulis extract
relationships.evidence_quote: Cold and mechanical allodynia induced by paclitaxel were significantly alleviated in the D. caulis 300 and 500 mg/kg group (Figure 3A,B).

relationships.subject: capsazepine
relationships.evidence_quote: When 1 μg/mouse of capsazepine, a TRPV1 receptor antagonist, was injected intrathecally, cold and mechanical allodynia were significantly alleviated (Figure 7).

relationships.subject: vicenin-2
relationships.evidence_quote: The behavioral assessment showed that cold and mechanical allodynia were greatly alleviated in the 10 mg/kg vicenin-2 administration group (Figure 6).

key_findings: Oral D. caulis extract relieved paclitaxel-induced cold and mechanical allodynia in mice and reduced the paclitaxel-induced rise in spinal TRPV1 mRNA and protein.
Vicenin-2 (about 0.245% of extract) and intrathecal capsazepine produced similar antinociceptive effects, suggesting spinal TRPV1 modulation.
